title_en: Healthcare Access for Work Pass Holders Renting a Room
summary_en: What healthcare cover a work-pass holder renting a room should have in place, and why it matters.
body_en:
Falling sick far from home is stressful enough without worrying about the bill. Knowing what cover you already have — and what you don't — matters before you need it, not after, when you're too unwell to make calls and ask questions.

What your employer must provide

For Work Permit and S Pass holders, MOM requires employers to buy and maintain medical insurance with coverage of at least S$60,000 per year, covering inpatient care and day surgery, including conditions that aren't work-related. This requirement was enhanced from 1 July 2023, and the cost cannot be passed on to you as the worker.

What this doesn't cover

  • It's generally focused on inpatient care and day surgery — everyday outpatient visits, like a polyclinic consultation for a cold, usually aren't included.
  • It doesn't replace work injury compensation cover, which is separate and required for workplace accidents.
  • Employment Pass holders should check their own employer's arrangement, since requirements and typical practice can differ by pass type.

What to check as a renter

  • Ask your employer directly what your medical insurance actually covers, and keep a copy or photo of the policy details.
  • Know which hospital or clinic network your insurance works with, so you're not figuring it out while unwell.
  • If you're unsure your coverage meets the current requirement, you can raise it with MOM directly.
  • Save your insurer's claim hotline number in your phone now, so you're not searching for it while unwell.

Fill the gap yourself if needed

If outpatient visits aren't covered, budget for them separately — a polyclinic visit is usually more affordable than a private GP. A little planning here means a sick day doesn't also become a financial shock on top of everything else.

General guidance, November 2026 — not legal advice. Check current requirements on mom.gov.sg.

facts_checked.claim: MOM requires employers to buy and maintain medical insurance of at least S$60,000 per year per Work Permit holder, covering inpatient care and day surgery, with the enhanced requirement effective from 1 July 2023 and extending to S Pass holders
